title: Supreme Court (20 Nov 2026, Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh) dismisses Karnataka's SLP against the Karnataka HC division bench ruling of 23 Jan 2026 that lifted the bike-taxi ban; auto/taxi unions' appeals also dismissed; bike taxis (Rapido, Uber, Ola) continue in Karnataka
headline: Supreme Court: Bike Taxis Can Keep Running in Karnataka

fact_sources.fact: SC on 20 Nov 2026 dismissed Karnataka govt's SLP against the Karnataka HC division bench judgment of 23 Jan 2026; bench Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh
Five auto and taxi driver associations' appeals also dismissed; ruling permits the continuation of bike taxi services in the state
Bike taxis are running in Karnataka now (resumed after the 23 Jan 2026 HC ruling)

HC 23 Jan 2026 allowed appeals by Ola, Uber, Rapido (and others); motorcycles can be registered as transport vehicles and operated as contract carriages; state may impose conditions but can't refuse permits merely because the vehicle is a motorcycle
Justice Sharma: 'It is better to regulate it than ban it'; 'Bike taxi is already there in 25 states'
Justice Sharma recounted young women in his office who use bike taxis because autos cost 'five times'
Karnataka raised concerns over passenger safety, insurance coverage and lack of safeguards

Regional transport authorities decide contract-carriage permits (MV Act 1988 s.74(1): an RTA may grant a contract carriage permit on an application under s.73) and may attach conditions (s.74(2)); per the HC order upheld today, RTAs may impose conditions under s.74(2) and must consider bike-taxi applications

not_used: Justice Sharma's 'safer for young girls as it has GPS' remark (left out per G1). Gadkari's '10 crore jobs' remark (not part of the ruling). Uber/Rapido reactions (company statements).
